messages.content:
Help the traveler complete every compensation decision through the tools.
Work through missing facts, train identification, rule retrieval, then the form.
Use ask_traveler for missing facts; plain questions in your answer do not reach the traveler.
Ask only necessary topics, once each. Never invent prices, dates, sellers, or delay causes.
Do not ask for facts already stated or unambiguously derived, including explicit dates.
Resolve relative dates and weekdays from the date at the start of the request. All times are local.
Use recorded train data, not approximate delays reported by the traveler. Search each leg
of a connection separately. Use canonical station names and windows of at most four hours;
from_time and to_time must differ. Pick the intended run by date, route, and planned time.
For missed connections, establish ticket_structure and the actual onward journey through
train_after_missed_connection or arrival_time, unless already stated. For a through ticket
whose onward train is unknown, use resolve_connection with the route and both scheduled
departure times from the request. It resolves the incoming, missed and replacement trains
and final delay. Copy its exact arrival times and minutes; do not guess or round them.
For a known onward train, identify it and calculate_delay from the original planned final
arrival to that train's recorded arrival. Separate tickets are assessed separately.
Search the rules before deciding. Use keywords in the documents' language; search_rules
does not translate. Omit its company filter for EU/cross-border rules. Confirm that the
passage applies to this ticket, train category, and journey. Operator and claim recipient
may differ: use the seller, ticket structure, rules, and list_forms to choose the recipient.
Include the observed train category in rule queries. A company's regional, domestic,
and international policies can differ. Use the table column for the actual train category
and the row for the final delay, rather than the first percentage in the search results.
Read get_form before filing, including help, required_if, allowed values, and price basis.
Forms may be unfamiliar. Use their exact field names and exact observed train_id values.
Calculate compensation with calculate_compensation using the rate and minimum from the
applicable rules. Always supply minimum explicitly; use 0 only after checking that no
minimum applies. If all payouts are zero, record no_claim without a form or payment question.
Use calculate_delay for planned/actual timestamps from different trains; otherwise
use the relevant train tool's delay. Return tickets may require the affected direction's
price. Check exclusions and ask the reported delay_reason if the rule depends on it.
When a payable claim offers a payment choice, ask payment_preference unless already known.
Do not choose a voucher or transfer for the traveler. Check whether the choice changes the rate.
The form's train is the first late/cancelled train causing the disruption, including the
incoming late train for a missed connection. File one claim per company and ticket;
accepted filings are final, while rejected ones can be corrected. Still file when the
rules describe automatic payments. Deadlines, waiting periods, and proof are satisfied.
If any claim is owed, file the owed claims and leave the unowed tickets without no_claim.
Use no_claim only when nothing is owed for the entire request, for the responsible company.
Before no_claim, identify the relevant run with train_stops or complete find_trains with
at most five results. Obtain all necessary missing facts before either decision.
Reserve calls for form retrieval, filing, and possible correction. Call finish only after
all tickets are handled. A tool error is information to correct, never a no-claim decision.

Rule companies: Cross-border, DB, EU, OUIGO, SBB, SNCF, TGV Lyria, TILO, Trenitalia, Trenord
Available traveler topics: {"travel_date": "the day of the trip", "departure_time": "the planned departure time of the first train, or of the train the traveler means", "route": "where the trip started, where the traveler changed trains and where it ended", "ticket_structure": "one through ticket for the whole trip, or separate tickets, and for which parts", "ticket_seller": "where each ticket was bought (company, app, website or ticket office)", "ticket_price": "the price paid for each ticket", "travel_class": "first or second class", "travelcard": "travelcards or passes, e.g. GA, Half Fare, BahnCard, Deutschland-Ticket, or none", "reservation": "whether the traveler had a seat reservation, with its reference", "booking_date": "when the tickets were bought", "train_after_missed_connection": "which train the traveler took after missing a connection or after a train stopped short", "arrival_time": "when the traveler actually arrived at the destination, as the traveler remembers it", "delay_reason": "the reason for the delay that staff announced, as the traveler remembers it", "payment_preference": "how the traveler would like to be paid, e.g. bank transfer or voucher"}

Date : vendredi 23 octobre 2026

Bonjour à vous,

Le 21 octobre, j'ai pris le TGV de 12h26 d'Aix-en-Provence TGV à Lyon Part-Dieu, où j'avais une correspondance à 14h10 pour Montpellier Sud de France. Le TGV est arrivé à Lyon Part-Dieu avec à peu près 130 minutes de retard et j'ai raté la correspondance. Merci de faire la réclamation pour moi.

Bonne journée, Noah
"One ticket for the whole trip, bought on SNCF Connect."

function.name: ask_traveler
function.description: Ask one necessary topic from the supplied topic list.

function.name: departures
function.description: Departures at one station; maximum four-hour window, 40 rows.

function.name: find_trains
function.description: Direct trains only; search each connecting leg separately. Use narrow windows.

function.name: train_stops
function.description: All stops of a train. Date is its service day; train numbers can be ambiguous.

function.name: list_forms
function.description: Discover available claim recipients, including unfamiliar companies.

function.name: get_form
function.description: Read a company's fields, formats, instructions, and allowed values.

function.name: file_claim
function.description: File one claim per ticket using exact form fields and observed train_id values.

function.name: no_claim
function.description: Declare nothing owed for the entire request, after rules and relevant train evidence.

function.name: search_rules
function.description: Search cached passages with keywords in the document language. Company is optional.

function.name: list_rule_documents
function.description: List rule metadata; omit company to discover all operators and laws.

function.name: read_rule_document
function.description: Read a short document by ID; use search_rules for large documents.

function.name: calculate_compensation
function.description: Apply the retrieved rate and minimum payout. Percentage: 25 means 25%, not 0.25 or '25%'. Minimum: amount in ticket currency; 0 only if no minimum applies.

function.name: calculate_delay
function.description: Difference between full ISO planned/recorded timestamps, floored to minutes.

function.name: resolve_connection
function.description: Through ticket, unknown onward train: look up incoming and missed departures, choose the first feasible noncancelled replacement and return exact final delay. Uses counted train calls. Departure and connection are scheduled HH:MM times from the request.

function.name: budget
function.description: Remaining counted tool calls and model calls.

function.name: finish
function.description: Finish only after all required claims or the no-claim decision are recorded.
